la:verb:peragro.gloss: to wander or travel through or over; pass through, traverse; spread through
senses: to wander or travel through or over; pass through, traverse; spread through
la:verb:peragro.html:
pĕr-ā^gro, āvi, ātum, 1 (
part. peragratus, in the dep. signif.; v.infra), v. a.
per and ager
, to wander or travel through or over, to go or pass through, traverse, etc. (class.; cf. percurro).
Lit.: provincias,.—Of bees: saltus silvasque,: loca avia,: in peragrandā Aegypto,: peragratis partibus,.—Of sailing: litora Liburnicis,: eques Romanus qui et commercia ea et litora peragravit,; ; .—
Dep. only in part.: peragratus omnes Germaniae partes, etc.,.—
Trop., to go through, traverse, to spread through; to search through, penetrate: omne immensum peragravit mente animoque,: eloquentia omnes peragravit insulas,: cujus res gestae omnes gentes terrā marique peragrassent,; ; .—Rarely with per: orator ita peragrat per animos hominum, ut, etc.,: gula peragrans,a roving appetite,.—Hence, * pĕrăgranter, adv., in roving about, .

la:verb:perago.html:
pĕr-ăgo, ēgi, actum (
inf. paragier, ), 3, v. a.
To thrust through, pierce through, transfix (only poet. and in post-Aug. prose): Theseus latus ense peregit,transpierced,: aliquem ardenti quercu,; cf.: externa peragi dextrā,.—Hence, transf., to kill, slay, .—
To pass through, traverse: freta,: cum sol duodena peregit Signa,.—
To drive about, harass, disturb, disquiet, agitate, annoy a person or thing (very rare): pecora peragens asilus,: totum Sempronium usque eo perago, ut, etc., Cael. ap. .—
To carry through, go through with, execute, finish, accomplish, complete, etc.
In gen. (class.; syn.: exsequor, conficio, patro): multum egerunt, qui ante nos fuerunt, sed non peregerunt,: carmen tubā solā peregit, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 508 Vahl.): fabulam,; cf. (and v. peractio): comitia,: concilium,: partes suas,: conata,: inceptum,: cursum,; cf.: coeptum iter,: dona,to finish distributing,: mandata, Ov. M. 7, 502: aetatem, vitam, aevum,; ; : facinus,; also, to exhaust: quot viros,.—Absol., = διάγειν, to pass one's life, .—Pass. impers.: Quis non peractum esse cum Pompeio crederet?that the war with Pompey is ended,.—
In partic., in jurid. Lat.: reum,to continue a prosecution till the defendant is condemned,; ; ; : accusationem,to prosecute to the end,: receptus est reus, neque peractus, ob mortem opportunam,.—
In gen., to work, or work up any thing.
Lit.: humum,to till, cultivate,: cibum,to digest,. —
Trop., to go through, go over, to relate, describe, detail, state: legatus peragit deinde postulata...Haec paucis verbis carminis concipiendique jurisjurandi mutatis peragit,: verbis auspicia,to mention,: res pace belloque gestas,to describe, treat of,: dum perago tecum pauca,: res tenues, tenui sermone peractas,delivered,.

pĕr-ambŭlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to ramble through, go through; to traverse, perambulate (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.: aedes,: multas terras,: omnium cubilia,: viridia,: rura,: astra,: terram,: universam insulam, et saep.—Pass.: perambulatum Romanis legionibus Niphatem,.—Poet.: frigus perambulat artūs,runs through,: recte necne crocum floresque perambulet Attae Fabula, si dubitem, rightly trod the stage (which was sprinkled with perfumed waters and strewed with flowers), i. e. was properly constructed, well written, : sermo perambulat,the fame spreads through,.—*
In partic., of a physician, to visit patients in succession, .—
To walk, conduct one's self (eccl. Lat.), ; .
